subject: Possible coef(mod, IRTpars = TRUE) calculation error

messages.author: c849e63a40bb8081
messages.subject: Possible coef(mod, IRTpars = TRUE) calculation error
parts:
Hi Phil,

I used an old version of MIRT until recently, and when I switched to version 1.21, my IRT coefficients are not being calculated correctly.  Here is some example code (my dataset has 12 items) that ran fine on ver 1.17.1:

mod3PLPost <- mirt(DCIcompPost,1, itemtype = '3PL', optimizer = 'NR', SE = TRUE, SE.type = "Louis")
coef3PLPost <- as.matrix(coef(mod3PLPost, IRTpars = TRUE, as.data.frame = TRUE))[1:48, ]
coef3PLPost <- matrix(as.vector(t(coef3PLPost)), nrow = 12, ncol = 12, byrow = TRUE)
colnames(coef3PLPost) <- c("Discr","Disc_2.5","Disc_97.5", "Diff","Diff_2.5","Diff_97.5", "Lower","Lower_2.5","Lower_97.5", "Upper", "Up_2.5","Up_97.5")
coef3PLPost[, c(1,4,7)]

However, with ver 1.21, a couple things seem to be happening.  1) The confidence intervals don't seem to be getting output as part of the coef() command (only the four main estimates).  2) The IRTpars = TRUE seems to have an error in the calculation for the typical IRT parameters (a, b,c).  Specifically, for the guessing parameter.  I know this becaus if you plot the model, the y-value for the item characteristic curves at low ability levels don't match the calculated guessing parameters (this is for ICCs that have flattened out at low ability levels).

Any ideas on what is happening?

Thanks,

Nick

Hi Nick,

Sounds funky. Could you provide a reproducible example? I'd be happy to check it out. If you have data that is too sensitive for a public forum then feel free to sent it to me directly. Cheers.

Phil
